metadata.title: Degradation vs Continuity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for determining when degraded operation is safer than full continuity or halt.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Resilience decision logic governing partial operation, constrained modes, and mission-essential continuity.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining when degraded operation is permitted and when full continuity is unsafe.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines degradation eligibility and continuity constraints as trust-relevant resilience data.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Continuity Planning controls (CP-2, CP-3, CP-7, CP-8) are constrained by degradation eligibility.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance requiring contextual evaluation for continued operation.

metadata.remarks: Degradation vs Continuity defines when partial or constrained operation is safer than full continuity or restoration. This pattern establishes non-equivalence between system availability and safe operational capability.

components.title: Degradation‑Eligible State
components.description: State in which reduced or constrained functionality can be provided without introducing new harm.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Essential functions may continue in alternate or degraded modes.

components.title: Continuity Exclusion
components.description: Conditions under which full continuity must not be pursued despite availability capability.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuity strategies consider unsafe or ineligible operating conditions.

components.title: Degraded Mode Definition
components.description: Explicit definition of reduced functionality modes and operational constraints.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate processing modes are explicitly bounded.

components.title: Degradation vs Continuity Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what continuity capability does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuity does not imply safety, correctness, or permission to operate normally.

components.title: Degradation Signaling
components.description: Emission of signals indicating degraded operation requirements or restrictions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Degraded operational states are visible and enforceable.
